Epson PowerLite 770F UST laser projector - landscape
[V] CAD unit price read Sep 18 2026 from Epson Canada. [U] selection / quantity; stock and rear-fabric test not confirmed.
PC CAD $1,500-2,500 plus two depth cameras, USB / power, mounts and shipping CAD $1,600-2,400 [U] budget allowance. Candidate: Orbbec Femto Bolt. Coverage / compatibility requires prototype.
[U] allowance; retains 15 x 8 ft wall panel. Image band is 15 x 4.5 ft. Sample-test UST performance.
Two landscape mounts and perimeter screen tensioning
[U] allowance: mounts 500-1,000 plus tensioning 300-800. Main tunnel structure excluded.
Two video feeds, adapters, power and network cables
[U] allowance: video 200-400 plus power / control 250-600. Do not use a mirroring splitter.
Rear-bay blackout / shipping CAD $700-1,800 plus commercial playback software / licensed animated raptor CAD $800-1,400 [U] budget. Actual licence and asset quotes not obtained.
[U] 25% contingency for a design still being tested. Edit percentage in A60.
Project Hours - Shared design, development and testing
Design 6-12 h + procurement 6-12 h: projection layout, two overhead depth cameras, position-to-frame mapping and sourcing.
Prototype 12-24 h: fabric / UST test plus camera coverage, camera handoff, visitor position and bidirectional video scrubbing.
Programming 28-56 h: projection playback 12-24 h plus tracking 16-32 h. Map one visitor position to video frame, smooth forward / reverse, hold when stopped, reset on exit / loss.
Integration 12-24 h: projector / camera mounts, USB and power, camera handoff calibration, projection alignment and media preparation. No custom PCB.
Testing 10-20 h: seams, brightness / colour, person walking / stopping / reversing, entry / exit, camera handoff and reverse playback performance.
QA 4-8 h: tracking loss / re-entry, restart recovery and soak setup / review. Unattended soak time is not billed.
Public deployment uplift x1.4: add 40% of base project hours, rounded up. Covers recovery, durable mounting / cabling and operator reliability.
Documentation 6-12 h: projection and camera layout, calibration, media / configuration backups and operator handover.

Content development 8-16 h: source an existing licensed animated raptor, make one side-view walking-across-wall clip, simple background, one review / revision and export for forward / reverse scrubbing. No bespoke modelling.
25% buffer on design + prototype + programming + integration + content after x1.4 uplift. Design-only hours are in A58.

Shared labour + shared hardware / projector 1 + contingency
Scope: one 15 x 4.5 ft wall, two landscape USTs, one raptor video and one tracked visitor. Two overhead depth cameras provisionally allowed.
Rate supplied by Garrett; edit C57. HST excluded.
LOW scenario. Base design-only hours in A58 feed the buffer. All labour hours are [U] planning estimates.
Overlap between the two 8 ft wide images: 1 ft [U]. Edit overlap in A59; combined width is calculated in D52.
Materials contingency: 25% [U]. Edit percentage in A60. Shared equipment and contingency are allocated to projector 1.
Nominal optical throw: 8 ft x 0.25 = 2 ft [U calculation]. Complete mounting / cooling / access envelope remains unverified.
Reserve 3-3.5 ft rear-bay depth provisionally [U]; verify model-specific mounting height and physical clearance before fabrication.
Use tensioned diffuse rear-projection fabric. Keep framing and exterior branding out of the beam paths and translucent screen back.
Assume familiar depth / playback tools, wired indoor installation. New technology adds x1.5-2 to affected work (not applied). Asset and camera compatibility unverified.
Excludes bespoke raptor modelling / rigging, additional scenes, multi-person following, audio / sound design, main tunnel fabrication and ongoing attendance.
Follow behaviour: map visitor position to clip frame. Stops hold a frame. Backward steps reverse the clip (raptor backpedals). Exit / lost tracking resets.
Prototype camera coverage, handoff and video scrubbing before committing. Calendar assumes 30 focused h/week, x1.3 approvals. Lead times and real hardware unverified.
